newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel arrests top Hamas activist heading to haj.
newsitem.headline: Israel arrests top Hamas activist heading to haj.

text.p: Israeli authorities arrested a leader of the Palestinian Islamic group Hamas on his way to the annual Moslem pilgrimage to Mecca, his family said on Thursday.
They said Sheikh Hassan Yousef, 43, was arrested on Tuesday trying to cross from the West Bank to Jordan. He was ordered held for four months without charges at a military prison in Israel.
Israeli officials were not immediately available to comment. Palestinians say Yousef belongs to the political wing of Hamas, a main opponent to Israeli-PLO peace moves.
"He was accompanying the haj mission and arrested at the border," Yousef's 16-year-old son Suhaib said by telephone. He said he did not know why his father was arrested.
Family members said Yousef had been jailed more than eight times during three decades of Israeli occupation and was among 400 Islamists banished by Israel to Lebanon for up to one year in 1992.

Hamas is a leading critic of Israeli-PLO peace moves. The group's military wing has carried out suicide bombings that have killed dozens of Israelis as part of what it calls "the armed struggle to liberate Palestine".
